name: Brawler
description:
The chair comes apart in your hands and you don't stop to think about it. Someone is in front of you and the problem requires solving immediately—a fist, a headbutt, whatever the nearest surface recommends. The bystanders have time to wince. You don't give yourself that luxury.

Brawlers don't fight elegantly. They don't fence, they don't strategize, and they don't wait. When a situation calls for violence, a Brawler's answer arrives before the question finishes being asked—fists first, details later. This isn't a failure of imagination; it's a philosophy. The Brawler has learned that the person who acts is almost always ahead of the person who plans, and that a bare fist lands just as hard as a carefully prepared strike from a fine blade.

What sets Brawlers apart from other hard-hitting fighters is where they draw their power from. Rather than imposing control on a fight, they thrive inside its disorder. Every blow exchanged nearby—whether they land it or not—feeds something in them, a rising energy they can spend on raw bonuses or pass along to allies as a surge of momentum. The noisier and more chaotic the battle, the stronger a Brawler becomes. A calm, controlled skirmish is their worst environment. A full brawl—multiple enemies, things breaking, everyone swinging at everyone—is their element.

Brawlers wear their wounds differently than other fighters. Where some combatants grow cautious as injuries mount, a Brawler hits their stride. When their Endurance drops below half, they become harder to hurt and more dangerous to face, tapping into a bloody-minded stubbornness that refuses to concede even the ground they're standing on. Tricks, magic, clever wordplay—the Brawler shrugs it all off with Strength, and regards enchanted gear with a superstitious contempt that occasionally motivates them to smash it outright, which, somehow, they find invigorating.

Play a Brawler if you want to:

  • Thrive in the thick of it, drawing power from chaos and violence rather than order and positioning.

  • Fight with your fists and whatever's near at hand, treating weapons as optional extras in a world where bare knuckles are already plenty.

  • Get hit, keep going, and hit back harder, turning injury and bad situations into a source of escalating danger rather than weakness.

Questions to consider when making a Brawler:

  • Where did they learn—or develop—this style? A rough upbringing, tavern fights, a pit-fighting circuit, a punishing martial discipline, or simply a life that kept putting them in situations where they had to figure it out?

  • How do they feel about their impatience? Is it something they've accepted, something they're working on, or something they actively lean into as a statement about how the world works?

  • What's their relationship to magic? Wary suspicion, outright contempt, fearful avoidance, or a deeper conviction that things that can't be punched shouldn't be trusted?

  • Do they have a code—rules about who they fight, how hard, and when they stop—or do they decide each time from scratch?

  • What's the fight that made them who they are? Did they win it?

novizio.abilities: Action Over Deliberation, Embrace The Chaos, Fists Up
